renders.prompt: Explain the argument of this song as if to a bright 10-year-old. Short words. Concrete images. No jargon, no Sanskrit terms, no meta-commentary.

paragraphs.text: We bow to the master of the moon-crest, his longing tucked away. We cannot do a thing, so his all-helping strength is our shelter -- there is no stand-in for him past all traits.

He stays one and boundless, yet his own dazzle fools us still. Love grows powers, sway, and an end of rebirth like green shoots. Already won, we still ask when he is won. He, the white swan, lodges only in clear hearts; his twin lamps wake us and warm us. He staged the triple play -- only the playwright can close it. He turns real and fake to naught or aught, bound and free in one.

paragraphs.text: Hail moon-crest master, hunger holstered. Useless at everything, so his help-all force is shelter -- no stand-in past all measure.

One, no edges, yet his own glare fools us daily. Devotion sprouts juice, juice-plus-sway, plus exit from rebirth. Bagged already, still asking when bagged. He squats solely in scrubbed hearts; twin lamps, one to see, one to burn. He set the triple stage -- only the playwright strikes it. Real, fake, delete, save -- bound and unbound in a single body.
